outcomes: Use coding agents to plan and complete substantial programming tasks.
Design effective context and tools for an agent, including custom skills and management of the context window.
Construct multi-agent workflows that decompose a task and orchestrate the parts.
Build a lightweight agent from its core components: a model, a tool-use loop, and context management.
Evaluate coding agents on real tasks with benchmarks and metrics, and interpret the results honestly.
Analyze what agents can and cannot do, how they fail, and what responsible use looks like.

class_format.what: A short video or reading on the day's idea.
A few quiz questions on that material, taken in the room.
About twenty minutes on one idea and the evidence behind it.
The instructor drives Claude Code on the projector, including the moments when it goes wrong.
Students build and measure something, and a checker script reports what is done and what is still missing.

lectures.title: Course Intro
lectures.summary: How the course works, what a coding agent is, and a first look at Claude Code and GitHub.

lectures.title: Foundations
lectures.summary: From neural networks to transformers to coding agents, then a first hands-on session in Claude Code.

lectures.title: Git, Verify, Deploy
lectures.summary: Driving Git and GitHub through the agent, giving the agent a check it can run, and deploying a site to GitHub Pages that is verified live.

lectures.title: Stochastic Outputs and In-Context Steering
lectures.summary: Why repeated runs of one prompt differ, why no single run proves anything, and how context and examples steer the output.

lectures.title: The Agentic Loop and Reasoning
lectures.summary: The loop an agent runs, and the reasoning methods layered on it (chain of thought, self-consistency, ReAct, Reflexion), measured against each other.

lectures.title: Prompting and Plan Mode
lectures.summary: Prompting as a skill, the explore, plan, code, commit workflow, and judging an agent's plan before it edits anything.

lectures.title: Review and Debug Agent Output
lectures.summary: Debugging with an agent: build a failing test first, rank hypotheses, demand evidence, and keep a human at the symptom, the ranking, and the merge.

lectures.title: Context Engineering
lectures.summary: The context window as a budget: measuring what fills it, and five moves that keep a long session sharp.

lectures.title: Memory Architectures
lectures.summary: Four kinds of agent memory, how each maps onto files an agent writes and re-reads, and why a remembered fact can go stale.

lectures.title: Tool Use
lectures.summary: What a model actually sees of a tool, four rules for designing reliable tools, and reliability measured over repeated runs.

lectures.title: Structured Generation
lectures.summary: A schema guarantees the shape of an answer but not its truth: constrained decoding, designing for missing data, and accuracy checked against a gold key.

lectures.title: Embeddings and Retrieval
lectures.summary: What keyword search, embeddings, and an agent with grep each miss, measured per question type on one gold set, and why a leaderboard score does not predict your own questions.

lectures.title: The RAG Pipeline
lectures.summary: Fusion, reranking, and cited answers each help on average and can hurt on a given dataset, so each stage is added and measured on its own and every citation is checked against its source.

lectures.title: RAG Evaluation
lectures.summary: Measuring retrieval and answers with recall@k, MRR, nDCG, and faithfulness, and deciding when to prompt, retrieve, or fine-tune.

modules.name: Extending agents: skills, MCP, and codebases

lectures.title: Skills
lectures.summary: Agent skills as reusable procedures that load only when they are needed, and writing one.

lectures.title: MCP
lectures.summary: The Model Context Protocol, its tool ecosystem and security basics, and building a server of your own.

lectures.title: Codebase and Hooks
lectures.summary: Agents on large codebases, spec-driven development, and deterministic guardrails written as hooks.

modules.name: Architectures, multi-agent systems, and building from scratch

lectures.title: Agent Architectures
lectures.summary: From ReAct to Reflexion to plan-and-solve, and when a fixed workflow beats an autonomous agent.

lectures.title: Multi-Agent Systems
lectures.summary: Orchestrator and worker designs, and a structured debate over when several agents actually beat one.

lectures.title: Build From Scratch I
lectures.summary: Writing a working agent loop directly against the model API, to understand the machinery.

lectures.title: Build From Scratch II and the Agent SDK
lectures.summary: Adding context management, memory, and error handling, then porting the agent to the Claude Agent SDK.

lectures.title: Reading Benchmarks Critically
lectures.summary: Construct validity and contamination, and how to read a coding-agent benchmark result with suspicion.

lectures.title: Evals Are Experiments
lectures.summary: Building an evaluation harness and reporting pass@k with error bars, variance, and statistical power.

lectures.title: LLM as Judge
lectures.summary: Where model graders are biased, how to check a grader, and evaluating the path an agent took versus only its outcome.

lectures.title: Open SOTA Discussion
lectures.summary: A student-driven discussion of the state of the art: responsible use, economics, and where the field is going.

lectures.title: Security and Guardrails
lectures.summary: The lethal trifecta, indirect prompt injection against students' own systems, and guardrails and approval gates as part of the design.

lectures.title: Demo Day (first session)
lectures.summary: Student groups present the products they built.

lectures.title: Demo Day (second session)
lectures.summary: The remaining groups present, and the semester closes.

projects.name: Personal website
projects.summary: A personal website built by directing Claude Code, deployed to GitHub Pages, and handed in with a decision log and proof that the live site works.

projects.name: RAG system
projects.summary: A question-answering system over a document collection, with keyword, embedding, and hybrid retrieval compared by recall@k, MRR, and nDCG on a hand-built gold set.

projects.name: Codebase with custom skills
projects.summary: An existing codebase extended with the student's own skills, hooks, and MCP servers, with a write-up of what was automated and how it was verified.

projects.name: Full-stack agent project
projects.summary: A working product built by a group of students around an agent for a real user, with one claim backed by a small evaluation and a threat model, presented at Demo Day.
